page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8481C processor operating at 2.7 GHz, the instance allocates 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, resulting in 2 threads per core. The CPU configuration includes a 105 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate a divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. The instance achieves average performance in single-core metrics, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1618.89 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1713.0. However, multi-core and memory-intensive benchmarks are generally weak. The stress-ng multi-core score is 3315.66, and the Geekbench multi-core score is 3813.0. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block bandwidth at 28.42 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 21.13 GB/sec.

Despite weak multi-core scaling, the processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512). These instructions assist in specific workloads; for example, LLM inference text generation using a small 135M model reaches an average speed of 112.11 tokens/sec, though prompt processing for the same model remains weak at 390.79 tokens/sec. Static web serving throughput is average at 6.68 GB/sec, while database operations and Redis SET operations register in the lower performance tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c3-standard-4 provides dedicated CPU resources and modern architectural features at a standard resource density, though its raw multi-threaded compute and memory throughput are low relative to the hardware class. It is best suited for workloads that benefit from single-threaded performance or specialized Intel AMX and AVX-512 instructions, such as lightweight web serving, basic text processing, and small-scale serialization tasks, rather than memory-bound databases or highly parallelized compilation.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-4 is an x86_64 general-purpose instance configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor running at 2.7 GHz with 2 physical cores, 2 threads per core, and a 105 MB L3 cache. The instance does not include local storage or GPU resources. Performance benchmarks show average single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1713.0 and static web serving throughput of 6.68 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are relatively weak, as seen in the stress-ng multi-core score of 3315.66 and a large-block memory read speed of 28.42 GB/sec. Supported hardware features include Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions, which assist in specific vector and matrix operations. This instance is suited for lightweight web serving, basic text processing, and workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation without high memory bandwidth demands.
